title: Linear polynomial fibre quotient under arbitrary base change
statement: Let A be a commutative integral domain and r a prime ideal of A[X] [def-weil-polynomial-ring], such that its canonical A-algebra residue field κ(r) [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a fraction field of A. Let S be any commutative A[X]-algebra, with the induced A-algebra structure. Put K=κ(0_A), R=K tensor over A with S, and let e : κ(r) ≃ₐ[A] K be the canonical isomorphism of fraction fields. Set ξ=e(image of X in κ(r)) and f=1 tensor (image of X in S) - ξ tensor 1. Then R/(f) [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] is ring-isomorphic to κ(r) tensor over A[X] with S. No completion, derivation, Noetherianity, nonzero-fibre, or contraction hypothesis is required.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07PU, second paragraph of the proof, displayed linear quotient identification

proof.text: Identify κ(r) and K with the canonical A-algebra equivalence IsLocalization.algEquiv for the nonzero-divisor submonoid. This uniquely determined isomorphism uses no existentially chosen algebraic data. Put ξ=e(X), R=K tensor over A with S, I=(1 tensor X - ξ tensor 1), and Q=R/I.

The maps κ(r) → Q given by the composite of e and the left inclusion followed by quotient, and S → Q given by the right inclusion followed by quotient, agree on A by their algebra-map laws and on X by the defining relation I. Polynomial.algHom_ext therefore shows that they agree on A[X]. The tensor universal property yields h : κ(r) tensor over A[X] with S → Q.

In the reverse direction, e inverse followed by the left inclusion into the fibre and the right inclusion from S give g : R → κ(r) tensor over A[X] with S. The tensor balancing relation for X shows g(f)=0. The ideal span criterion and quotient universal property give gq : Q → κ(r) tensor over A[X] with S.

For a pure tensor k tensor s in R, h(g(k tensor s)) is the quotient class of k tensor s, since e and e inverse cancel and (k tensor 1)(1 tensor s)=k tensor s. Tensor induction and quotient induction give h composed with gq equal to identity. The same pure-tensor calculation in the fibre gives gq composed with h equal to identity. Assemble the ring equivalence. This covers S=0 and all zero fibres because the proof uses no nontriviality of S or the tensors.

lean.statement:
theorem linear_fiber_quotient
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    (r : Ideal (Polynomial A)) [r.IsPrime] [IsFractionRing A r.ResidueField]
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra (Polynomial A) S] [Algebra A S]
    [IsScalarTower A (Polynomial A) S] :
    let K := (⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField
    let R := (⊥ : Ideal A).Fiber S
    let e : r.ResidueField ≃ₐ[A] K :=
      IsLocalization.algEquiv (nonZeroDivisors A) r.ResidueField K
    let ξ := e (algebraMap (Polynomial A) r.ResidueField X)
    let f : R := Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (algebraMap (Polynomial A) S X) -
      Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft (S := A) ξ
    Nonempty ((R ⧸ Ideal.span ({f} : Set R)) ≃+* r.Fiber S)
